name: Fresh and frozen fruit
anchor: Per-produce-class sovereign maximum levels for lead and cadmium (EU Reg. 2023/915 and Switzerland VHK 817.022.15; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2; AU-NZ Schedule 19; MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel MOH FCS-2016), nickel under EU Reg. 2024/1987, total and inorganic arsenic under MERCOSUR and Israel MOH FCS-2016, and total mercury under Hong Kong Cap. 132V and Israel MOH FCS-2016.
native_basis_label: fresh or frozen fruit as sold, wet weight, edible portion after washing and removal of stones, stems and inedible peel
scope_note: Whole and cut fresh fruit and individually quick-frozen fruit: pome fruit, stone fruit, citrus, berries and small fruit, grapes, tropical and subtropical fruit, and melons. Freezing does not change the water content materially, so frozen fruit shares the fresh wet-weight basis. OUT OF SCOPE: dried and dehydrated fruit (dried-fruit row, a different basis); fruit snacks, purees, leathers, jams and compotes (fruit-snacks row); fruit juices, nectars and fruit drinks (Category 5 Beverages); canned fruit in hermetically sealed tinplate (Category 7 canned-foods-general, which carries the tin maximum level); table olives (pickled-fermented-vegetables row); fruiting vegetables such as tomato, pepper, aubergine and cucurbits, which are botanically fruits but which every sovereign schedule classes as fruiting vegetables (non-root-vegetables row); tree nuts and dried pulses (Categories 28 and 27); products marketed for ages 0 to 5, which route to Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule. COLLAPSED SOVEREIGN SPLITS: the sovereign schedules split this row for lead (Hong Kong, Switzerland and MERCOSUR set 200 ug/kg for cranberries, currants, elderberries and strawberry-tree fruit against 100 ug/kg for other fruit) and for cadmium (Switzerland sets 20 ug/kg for pome, stone and citrus fruit, 30 ug/kg for berries and small fruit, 40 ug/kg for raspberries and 50 ug/kg for other fruit). The row binds the strictest member value in each case, so berry and cranberry products certify against a bar stricter than their own sovereign class value.
basis_guard: wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|as listed|product as offered to consumer|product as placed on market|as sold|as_sold|as consumed|commodity|edible part
basis_guard_note: Every named anchor for this row must sit in a dietary as-sold, wet-weight, edible-part or portion-ordinarily-consumed basis. The guard rejects the register's article and material bases (toy and food-contact migration, textile and leather extraction, fertiliser and growing-media dry matter, colour-additive ingredient specifications, animal-feed 12 percent moisture), any one of which would be a basis conflation if it anchored a food row.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only; the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for the row's product form in the row's native basis, a disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination, or a control; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.basis: wet weight, fresh fruit as sold
Pb.label: Five independent credible regulators converge on 100 ug/kg lead for fresh fruit (Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 9, AU-NZ Schedule 19, Switzerland VHK Obst, MERCOSUR GMC 12/2011 with Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019, Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3); the berry carve-outs at 200 ug/kg are named so the collapsed split is visible.
Pb.substantiation: Direct maximum levels for the exact product form in the row's native basis. The berry and cranberry rows at 200 ug/kg are the government-written carve-outs for the accumulating small-fruit species; because one HMTc value must hold across the whole row, the row binds 100 ug/kg and cranberry, currant and elderberry products certify against a value stricter than their own sovereign class. The AU-NZ row is applied on the fresh basis only; Schedule 19 calculates dried and dehydrated foods on the pre-drying basis, which is why it is not carried into the dried-fruit row. AUDIT DISPOSITIONS (from the broader register review rather than this row's scan, which returned no stricter-unselected rows): two stricter Hong Kong rows exist that are not applicable to fresh fruit. 'Tomatoes, preserved by heat treatment and hermetically sealed' (50 ug/kg) is a heat-sterilised canned tomato product and routes to Category 32 tomato-condiments. 'Canned chestnuts and canned chestnuts puree' (50 ug/kg) is a canned tree-nut product and routes to Category 28. MERCOSUR's 'fruit-based ice cream' rows (lead 70, cadmium 50, total arsenic 100) are a frozen dessert form and are not fresh fruit; no frozen-dessert row exists anywhere in the taxonomy, which is recorded as a taxonomy gap.

Cd.basis: wet weight, fresh fruit as sold
Cd.label: Switzerland VHK 817.022.15 sets 20 ug/kg cadmium for pome fruit, stone fruit, citrus fruit and mango, the strictest sovereign cadmium maximum level applicable to any product in this row; MERCOSUR, Paraguay and Israel set 50 ug/kg for fresh fruit generally.
Cd.substantiation: The Swiss annex mirrors EU Reg. 2023/915 and carries the per-class cadmium rows that the register's EU coverage lacks. Pome, stone and citrus fruit are the largest members of this row by volume, so 20 ug/kg is not a marginal member value. Berries at 30 ug/kg, raspberries at 40 ug/kg and residual fruit at 50 ug/kg are the government-written splits; the row binds the strictest, and those looser classes certify against a stricter bar.

tAs.basis: wet weight, fresh fruit as sold
tAs.label: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 set total arsenic for fresh fruit, berries and small fruit at 300 ug/kg; Israel MOH FCS-2016 sets 1000 ug/kg for the same commodity class.
tAs.substantiation: Direct total-arsenic maximum levels for fresh fruit in an as-offered basis. Total arsenic is reported for its own sake and is never satisfied by the inorganic-arsenic cell; the inorganic-arsenic species limit for this row (60 ug/kg) is far stricter and is the operative arsenic constraint.

iAs.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3 sets the only inorganic-arsenic maximum level any credible government writes for fruits and vegetables (60 ug/kg); the EU, Codex, FDA, AU-NZ, Hong Kong and Swiss instruments set inorganic-arsenic maximum levels only for rice, juices, seaweed and infant food.
iAs.substantiation: Inorganic arsenic is the health-relevant arsenic species and is never satisfied by the total-arsenic cell; both are reported. This value is a direct maximum level for the product class, not a read-across, and it sits well below the total-arsenic ceiling for the same row, so the species cell is the binding arsenic constraint in practice.

tHg.basis: wet weight, fresh fruit as sold
tHg.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3 sets total mercury for fruits and vegetables at 30 ug/kg, the only sovereign total-mercury maximum level whose scope reaches fresh fruit.
tHg.substantiation: Direct maximum level for the commodity class. Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 12 sets a stricter 10 ug/kg but its scope is 'vegetables, other than edible fungi' and does not reach fruit, so it is not applicable to this row; it binds the four vegetable rows and the pickled row instead.

MeHg.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury maximum level for this product form: the routed corpus reports no methylmercury measurement in this matrix, and the only credible methylmercury maximum levels in force (US FDA CPG 540.600; HK Cap. 132V item 11) are scoped to fish, shellfish and crustaceans, so neither supplies an applicable ceiling for a fruit. Methylmercury is therefore held under mandatory analytical control rather than recorded not-material, and it remains bounded by identity below the published total-mercury ceiling for this row (methylmercury cannot exceed total mercury). No methylmercury ceiling is invented.
MeHg.reference_method: Methylmercury by GC-ICP-MS or EN 16801, required only on a lot whose total mercury reaches 60 percent of the published total-mercury ceiling; any quantifiable methylmercury on such a lot is investigated and the lot is held pending root-cause analysis.

Ni.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a nickel maximum level for fruit. EU Reg. 2024/1987, the only comprehensive dietary nickel instrument in existence, enumerates leafy, fruiting, brassica, root, tuber, bulb and legume vegetables, fresh herbs, cereals, pseudocereals, pulses, tree nuts, seeds, cocoa, seaweed and juices, and deliberately sets no maximum level for fruit; the Swiss VHK nickel rows mirror it and likewise omit fruit. Because no instrument reaches the commodity at all, HMTc publishes no nickel number for fresh fruit rather than borrowing the fruiting-vegetable value of 400 ug/kg from a different commodity class.
Ni.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on every lot as part of the mandatory eight-totals panel. Investigate any result above 400 ug/kg (the EU fruiting-vegetable maximum level, used here only as an investigation trigger and not as a certification ceiling) against orchard soil, foliar-spray and stainless-steel processing provenance before release.

Sn.rationale: Every tin maximum level in the register is scoped to canned product: EU Reg. 2023/915 sets 200000 ug/kg for canned foods and 100000 ug/kg for canned beverages, Codex CXS 193-1995 and AU-NZ Schedule 19 set 250000 ug/kg for canned foods, and Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets 250000 ug/kg for canned food other than canned beverages. Those limits regulate one contamination pathway, dissolution of tin from tinplate into the packed food. This row is not packed in tinplate, so the pathway that every sovereign tin limit addresses is physically absent and any tin present is dietary background rather than packaging migration. Fresh and frozen fruit is sold loose, in fibre punnets, in film or in polymer trays. Hermetically sealed tinplate presentations of this commodity route to the canned-foods row in Category 7 and carry the canned-foods tin maximum level there.
Sn.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every lot as part of the mandatory eight-totals panel; a result above 50 ug/kg is investigated for a metal-contact source in harvest, wash, transport or packing before the lot is released.
Sn.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a tin maximum level for non-canned produce; all tin maximum levels in the register are conditioned on a canned (tinplate) presentation, and the EU rows expressly exclude canned dried and canned powdered products from even that scope.
Sn.jurisdictions_checked: EU Reg. 2023/915; EU Reg. 2024/1987 (nickel); Switzerland VHK 817.022.15 (2026 metal/metalloid annex); Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule; AU-NZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel MOH FCS-2016; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR, action levels)

Al.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for any fruit, vegetable or produce form in any jurisdiction. The register's aluminium limits are drinking-water and bottled-water parameters, infant-formula maximum levels, a food-contact plastics specific migration limit, toy migration limits, and permitted-additive levels for baked and starch foods; none of them regulates aluminium as a contaminant of produce. Aluminium is also the third most abundant element in the earth's crust and appears in produce largely as soil-derived and root-associated mineral content rather than as process contamination, so no near-neighbour read-across is supportable either. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone aluminium number for this row.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every lot, reported to the applicant. Document any aluminium-containing processing aid, packaging contact or anti-caking agent, comply with the additive rules of every market of sale, and investigate any result that is an outlier against the applicant's own lot history.

Cr.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a total-chromium maximum level for this product form. The only dietary total-chromium maximum levels in the register are Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7 for vegetables (500 ug/kg) and pulses, cereals, meat, fish and dairy powder rows under the same item, plus drinking-water and color-additive specifications. The Hong Kong vegetable row does not reach fruit, and no jurisdiction writes a total-chromium maximum level for fruit. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone total-chromium number for this row; total chromium is screened on every lot and hexavalent chromium is controlled by reflex speciation.
Cr.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every lot; investigate any elevated result against soil, irrigation water and processing-equipment provenance and reflex-speciate per the Cr-VI control.

Cr-VI.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum level for any food in any jurisdiction, and this row has no published total-chromium parent to bound the species against (the only total-chromium food maximum level in the register, Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7, is scoped to vegetables and does not reach this product form). With neither a species limit nor a published parent, HMTc publishes no hexavalent-chromium number and controls the species by mandatory reflex speciation.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every lot. Any total-chromium result at or above 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation by EN 15192 or EPA 6800 IC-ICP-MS isotope dilution; any quantifiable Cr(VI) at LOQ fails the lot and the lot is held pending root-cause analysis.
Cr-VI.bounded_by: Cr (total chromium, itself a control for this row)
